title: Checkpoint capture of task state (foundational)
description: Signature original: At safe points between stages, the manager serializes the full task state: completed stages, pending work items, and intermediate results. Checkpoints are written atomically, so a crash mid-write never leaves a half checkpoint that looks complete. The state is plain JSON, inspectable without special tooling. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import json
state = {'stage': 2, 'done': ['crawl', 'index'], 'pending': ['rank'], 'results': {'hits': 42}}
blob = json.dumps(state)
print('checkpoint bytes:', len(blob))
print('restored stage:', json.loads(blob)['stage'])
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Session Continuity Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Resume validation before restart (foundational)
description: Signature original: Before resuming, the manager validates the checkpoint: schema check, checksum match, and a freshness test against the archive's current state. A checkpoint that fails validation is rejected outright rather than resumed into a corrupted task. Validation is what makes resume safe instead of merely convenient. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
import hashlib, json
state = {'stage': 2}
blob = json.dumps(state)
cp = {'blob': blob, 'sum': hashlib.sha256(blob.encode()).hexdigest()}
ok = hashlib.sha256(cp['blob'].encode()).hexdigest() == cp['sum']
print('checkpoint valid:', ok, '-> resume' if ok else '-> restart from scratch')
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Session Continuity Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Progress restoration without redo (foundational)
description: Signature original: On resume, completed stages are skipped and their cached intermediate results reloaded; only pending stages execute. The manager diffs the checkpoint's pending list against the plan to catch stages added since the checkpoint was written. This guarantees no work is repeated and no new work is silently dropped. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
plan = ['crawl', 'index', 'rank', 'report']
checkpoint_done = {'crawl', 'index'}
remaining = [s for s in plan if s not in checkpoint_done]
print('skipping completed:', sorted(checkpoint_done))
print('resuming with:', remaining)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Session Continuity Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Multi-device session handoff (foundational)
description: Signature original: Checkpoints are stored server-side under a session token, so a task started on one device can resume on another by presenting the token. The handoff transfers state only, never credentials, and the token expires after use or a timeout. This makes long investigations portable across the user's devices. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
sessions = {}
def handoff(state):
    import secrets
    tok = secrets.token_hex(4)
    sessions[tok] = state
    return tok
tok = handoff({'stage': 3})
print('handoff token:', tok, '| resumes at stage', sessions[tok]['stage'])
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Session Continuity Manager, 2026-10-21.

title: Session expiry and cleanup (foundational)
description: Signature original: Checkpoints expire after a configurable idle period, and expired sessions are deleted in a cleanup sweep. Expiry prevents stale state from being resumed into an archive that has moved on, which would produce subtly wrong results. The sweep logs what it removed so users can see that a session aged out. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example. Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH).
demo:
# Signature-authored original (JAH).
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
sessions = {'s1': datetime(2026, 10, 15), 's2': datetime(2026, 10, 21)}
now = datetime(2026, 10, 21, 12)
ttl = timedelta(days=3)
expired = [s for s, t in sessions.items() if now - t > ttl]
print('expired sessions cleaned:', expired)
provenance: Signature-authored original by Justin Addam Higgins (JAH) for Session Continuity Manager, 2026-10-21.
